missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Живот' is a masculine noun in the nominative as the subject of 'болит'. 'У меня' shows whose belly hurts. The standard way to complain of a stomachache.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Живот' is the accusative direct object of 'держит'; for this inanimate masculine noun the accusative equals the nominative. 'Руками' is the instrumental of means.
Strategic focus: Genitive after negation. 'Живота' is the genitive form of 'живот' after 'нет'. 'Большого' agrees in the masculine genitive. A natural way to describe a flat stomach.
Strategic focus: Dative recipient. 'Животу' is the dative form of 'живот', the recipient of harm from 'вредит'. 'Тяжёлая еда' is the nominative subject. A useful health expression.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'Животе' is the prepositional form of 'живот' after 'на', describing lying on one's stomach. A common everyday body position.

Strategic focus: Instrumental after 'под'. 'Животом' is the instrumental form of 'живот' after 'под', locating the belt below the belly. 'Пояс' is the nominative subject. Practises spatial instrumental.
Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Живот' is the nominative subject of 'стал'. 'Круглым' is the instrumental complement describing the resulting state. 'После обеда' uses the genitive 'обеда'.

missions.phrase: Дети смеются и держатся за животы.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative plural with 'за'. 'Животы' is the accusative plural of 'живот' after 'держаться за', the laughing-so-hard idiom. 'Дети' is the nominative plural subject.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural after 'на'. 'Животы' is the accusative plural of 'живот' after 'смотреть на'. 'Пациентов' is the genitive plural showing whose bellies. A clinical scene.

Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Животы' is the nominative plural of 'живот', the subject. 'Большие' is the agreeing plural adjective, and 'у толстых людей' uses genitive plural. Descriptive plural practice.
